transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I... I came in because my mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things anymore. Even writing a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—the numbers and words just sort of scatter on me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yes… most days. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even when my wife is being kind, it feels like I’m… far down somewhere, like at the bottom of a well.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About three weeks now… since my older sister died.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety lately?
Yes… slower. Everything feels slowed down. Getting out of a chair, answering someone… it’s like my body and even my tongue are moving through wet cement.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t done much physically?
I… I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying much attention to that. Some days I feel worn out, but I’m not sure what to make of it.
Have you been feeling guilty or blamed yourself for things more than usual lately?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say more than usual. I just… I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to?

Yeah… I suppose so. I haven’t touched the wood pieces sitting on my bench. I’ve skipped choir planning and chess, too.

Even fishing… usually I’d look forward to that, but lately it just sounds like more trouble than it’s worth. That’s… not really like me.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately—like when you’re trying to read or follow a conversation?

Yes… that’s actually part of why I came in. My mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things.

I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words or numbers just… scatter. I can’t keep them straight.
Have you noticed any days where your movements or actions felt almost painfully slow, or where you felt so restless that you couldn’t stay still?

Yes… slow, mostly. Everything takes me longer than it should.

Getting out of a chair, walking across the room… even answering you now, it feels like my body and my mouth are moving through wet cement.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or not wanting to live anymore?

…Yes. I don’t like saying that.

I keep thinking my family might be better off without me. And when I’m near the workshop, I get… scared of where my thoughts could go if I were left alone.
